topic: LabLLM: Teaching Tiny Language Models to Think on macOS

key_points: Primary source: free, native macOS app (Swift/SwiftUI) that puts the entire LLM training workflow in one place
Build a Transformer from scratch, train on your own datasets, use Apple Silicon + MLX for local training
Watch training metrics and loss curves live; save and resume checkpoints
Fine-tune with LoRA / DPO; inspect tokens and embeddings; experiment with sampling and generation; chat with the model you trained
No cloud, no subscription, no data leaving the Mac; MIT licensed
Requirements: macOS 14+, Apple Silicon M1 or newer, Xcode 15+, Swift Package Manager; pins mlx-swift to 0.31.6
Modes: Simple, Advanced, Expert; GPT-style decoder presets (tiny/small/medium/large-ish); char, byte, and trained BPE tokenizers
Training: pretraining (AdamW/SGD, warmup, cosine LR, gradient clipping, gradient accumulation), SFT with chat templates and assistant-only loss masking, LoRA, DPO
Export: 4-bit and 8-bit quantized model export; local OpenAI-shaped HTTP server with streaming responses
Beta software (Beta 0.1 'Teach Tiny Brains' 2026-08-15, Beta 0.2 'Remember the Run' 2026-08-18); 76 stars, created 2026-08-15
Educational macOS app by Felix Rieseberg that explains AI foundations by building a small model from scratch
Choose a tokenizer and training data, watch loss fall during pre-training, teach the model to answer questions, chat with a model that exists only on your Mac
Requires Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or later; notarized build, self-updates via Sparkle
Positioned as 'build a small version yourself' to demystify AI
Train a 1.5M parameter GPT-style language model on a MacBook Pro in under 10 minutes
End-to-end pipeline from raw text to working interactive LLM, built for Apple Silicon using MLX
Config: d_model 128, n_layers 7, n_heads 4, vocab 1024, seq_len 256; SentencePiece BPE tokenizer
Uses TinyStories dataset; expected perplexity ~9-15 on validation after 5-10 min training
Inspired by Sean Goedecke's guide: ~1.8M params trained on ~20M TinyStories tokens reaches perplexity ~9.6 in ~5 min on M1 Pro
Python-based (not a GUI app), requires macOS 13.5+, 16GB RAM
Hands-on course for systems engineers to understand LLM inference end to end (serving counterpart to CMU's Needle)
Build the path that loads a Qwen3 model, turns tokens into logits, and generates text
Built on MLX arrays and MLX extension runtime without high-level neural-network layers
Four-week learning path covering attention, RoPE, GQA, RMSNorm/MLP, KV cache, quantization, fused kernels, continuous batching, paged attention, MoE, speculative decoding
Focus is inference/serving, not training a model from scratch in a GUI
Guide to fine-tuning small language models with Apple MLX on your Mac in 30 minutes
Covers setup, dataset prep, LoRA training, and running inference locally
Apple Silicon unified memory lets a 16GB M3 MacBook Pro hold and train a 7B model — impossible on a discrete GPU with 8GB VRAM
MLX built from scratch for Apple Silicon, unlike PyTorch MPS which has backend quirks
Requirements: M1+ Mac, macOS 13.5+, 16GB RAM (32GB+ for 7B), Python 3.11+; no NVIDIA GPU, CUDA, Docker, or cloud needed

stats.fact: LabLLM is a free, open-source (MIT) native macOS app built in Swift/SwiftUI on Apple's MLX framework; it can train GPT-style models from scratch, fine-tune with LoRA/DPO, and chat with the result — all locally on Apple Silicon.
LabLLM requires macOS 14+, Apple Silicon M1 or newer, Xcode 15+, and Swift Package Manager; it pins mlx-swift to 0.31.6.
LabLLM supports pretraining (AdamW/SGD, warmup, cosine LR, gradient clipping, gradient accumulation), SFT with chat templates and assistant-only loss masking, LoRA, and DPO preference training.
LabLLM exports 4-bit and 8-bit quantized models and serves a local OpenAI-shaped HTTP endpoint with streaming responses.
LabLLM is beta software: Beta 0.1 'Teach Tiny Brains' released 2026-08-15, Beta 0.2 'Remember the Run' released 2026-08-18; ~76 GitHub stars as of research date.
A ~1.8M-parameter GPT-style transformer trained on ~20M TinyStories tokens reaches a perplexity of ~9.6 and produces coherent short stories in about 5 minutes on an M1 Pro.
A 1.5M-parameter GPT model (d_model 128, 7 layers, 4 heads, vocab 1024) trains on TinyStories in 5-10 minutes on Apple Silicon with MLX, reaching validation perplexity ~9-15.
Apple Silicon unified memory lets a 16GB M3 MacBook Pro hold and train a 7B model in memory — impossible on a discrete GPU with 8GB VRAM.
On dense 3-8B models, MLX runs 1.4-1.6x faster than llama.cpp at equivalent quantization; on MoE architectures the advantage reaches 3x.
On an M4 Max (546 GB/s memory bandwidth), MLX achieves ~525 tok/s on Qwen3-0.6B, ~159 tok/s on Qwen3-4B, and ~93 tok/s on Qwen3-8B at 4-bit quantization.

angles: LabLLM is the only native macOS GUI that wraps the full 'build → train → fine-tune → chat' loop in one app, vs. Python-script competitors (LocalMacLLM) or inference-only courses (tiny-llm)
Zero-cloud, zero-subscription, privacy-first positioning: everything stays on your Mac — a strong angle for privacy-conscious developers
Educational 'teach tiny brains to think' framing: watch loss curves bend and samples evolve live, making LLM internals tangible
Apple Silicon + MLX as the enabler: unified memory removes the VRAM ceiling, so a laptop can train real models
From-scratch GPT building with Simple/Advanced/Expert modes lowers the barrier for beginners while keeping deep controls for experts
Fine-tuning depth (SFT, LoRA, DPO) plus quantized export and local OpenAI-compatible serving makes it a practical local dev tool, not just a toy
Beta-stage honesty: clear 'not a production platform' caveat builds trust and sets realistic expectations
